11. At this stage, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that, execution of 5 deeds in the office of 2 different Sub-Registrar's Office on the same date i.e. on 3-6-1981, proved that, the defendants have resorted to fraud and forgery in executing these deeds. Otherwise, he submits, why the executant should execute and register the deed Nos. 3038 and 3029 in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Kalampur, Dhamrai, Dhaka, although the property is situated within the jurisdiction of Savar Sub-Registrar office. In reply to this submission, the learned Advocate for the opposite party argues that, as per section 28 of the Registration Act, execution of these 2 deeds at Kalampur Sub-Registrar Office was permitted by law (at that line) and in support of his contention he has referred to 37 DLR (AD) 177: Syed Kawsar Ali vs Gahar Kazi and others. Besides, the learned Advocate for the opposite party submits that, the case of the defendant has duly been proved by submitting relevant DCR, mutation khatian, Khajna Dhakilas etc. and as well as the defendants have submitted all 5 original kabala deeds and all these were duly proved and were marked as exhibits by the trial court. He next refers to the examination of DW 4, Hazi Habibur Rahman, who has deposed in the trial court stating that, there was a dispute between the defendants and one Helal Uddin, who purchased some property of the deceased Rakhal Chandra Mondal from his second wife Sagor Bewa (Step-mother of the plaintiff) and a complaint case was filed before the Martial Law Court in the year 1982 and the dispute was referred to the Savar Union Parishad and the Union Parishad had resolved the dispute in an amicable settlement and the defendants got 1.83 decimals of land. As such, it will be evident from the evidence on record, in all the forums and in all cases, including the case filed for permanent injunction and before the Martial Law Court, the defendants have appeared and contested to protect their title in the suit property, since they are the bonafide purchaser for value. He next submits that, in cross examination of the deposition of Laxmi Bewa, she was asked as to whether she was willing to sent her thumb impression for expert opinion, but she did not sent the same, although she had agreed to sent, because if the same were sent for expert opinion, then it would have been revealed that she herself had executed all these disputed 5 sale deeds. He therefore, concludes that, this Rule has no merit and the same may kindly be discharged. 

 16. On the contrary, the plaintiff's oral evidence are not supported by any documen-tary evidence, like Khatian or Khajna Dakhila and he has utterly failed to discharge the burden of proof that rested on him. Besides, as has been rightly pointed out by the trial court, and concurred with by the appellate court, the plaintiff has falsely claimed that he was in possession of the suit property. It was found by both the courts bellow that, the plaintiff's suit was liable to be dismissed under the provisions of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, for not seeking consequential relief by way of recovery of khas possession, which is, in my considered opinion, is correct opinion of the courts below.
